## Summary

- The Console can set or clear a User's Role. The change applies on the next request and does not invalidate Sessions or personal access tokens. The system identity cannot receive a Role. The last active local super admin cannot leave that Role.
- A personal access token can be created with no expiry. `expires_at` null does not expire. A non-null value must still be later than now. Existing tokens keep the expiry they already have.
- An Entity data page ordered by `row_id` runs in one query block through a security-definer function owned by the profile-view owner. A filter that is not leakproof, on a profile whose predicate depends on the row, is read from the barrier view. The signed access context is unchanged.
- The channel run detail page fills the console viewport. The execution index, the graph, and the node inspector share one row when the workspace is wide enough, and stack when it is not. The inspector does not cover the graph.
- Schedule lists show Enabled and do not change it. Create and edit still set `enabled`.

## Operator notes

- Upgrade from v0.6.0. v0.1.6 and v0.1.9 were tagged and are not installable. Do not install them.
- No new keys in `.env.example`. Leave the live `.env` in place. `ENTITY_OWNER_PASSWORD` and `ENTITY_READER_PASSWORD` remain required, URL-safe, and distinct.
- Compose still mounts named volume `refraq_pg` at `/var/lib/postgresql`. Default PGDATA is `/var/lib/postgresql/18/docker`. A site already on that mount, including one upgraded through v0.1.10, v0.2.0, v0.3.0, v0.4.0, v0.5.0, or v0.6.0, keeps its cluster. A site that only used the published v0.1.8 asset must still copy the anonymous-volume cluster onto `refraq_pg` before `up -d`, using the command in the v0.1.10 notes. Do not run `docker compose down -v`. Do not restore `/var/lib/postgresql/data`.
- Replace `docker-compose.yaml`, then `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`. The new image tag recreates `ensure-entity-db` (`restart: "no"`). That one-shot still prepares `entity_data`, `entity_access`, `acl`, `channel_dataset`, and `entity_change_log`. It installs `entity_access.profile_page` and `entity_access.profile_page_sql`. It does not create another schema and does not delete Entity rows. api and worker still refuse to start while any of those five schemas is missing.
- API start runs Foundation Upgrade `0085_pat_expires_nullable`. It makes `user_pats.expires_at` nullable. Existing rows keep their timestamps. It does not delete tokens, catalog rows, Entity rows, channel rows, or run records.
- `PATCH /users/{id}/role` requires `users:write`. `role_id` null clears the Role. A missing Role is `400` `USER_INVALID_ROLE`. The system identity is `409` `USER_SYSTEM_IMMUTABLE`. The last active local User on `super_admin` is `409` `USER_LAST_LOCAL_SUPER_ADMIN` when the new Role is not that Role. Sessions and personal access tokens stay valid. The next request uses the current `users.role_id`.
- `POST /tokens` still requires `expires_at`. `null` means the token does not expire. A non-null value that is not later than now is `400` `TOKEN_INVALID_EXPIRES_AT`. Omitting the field is `422` `REQUEST_INVALID`. Authentication treats a null expiry as not expired. A past expiry, a deactivated token, and a soft-deleted token remain `401` `AUTH_PAT_INVALID`. MCP tool arguments and results are unchanged. Webhook delivery is unchanged.
- Rolling back to an older compose after this migration is not supported. Downgrade of `0085` restores `NOT NULL` and fails while any token has a null expiry.
